name: Apostil
classification_notes: A simple hand-lettering script offered in three weights, closer to informal handwriting than a formal calligraphic script.
summary: A simple hand-lettering script in three weights from Hannes Famira's Brooklyn studio.
description: Apostil keeps to a straightforward, informal hand-lettered structure rather than a tight calligraphic system, giving it a versatile, approachable feel across its three weights.
foundry_blurb: Famira Fonts presents Apostil as a simple hand lettering font in three weights, distributed through Type Network alongside the rest of the studio's retail library.

name: Augustinian
classification_notes: A single-weight distressed serif built from a historic Dutch body-text sample, closer to a text serif revival than a display face despite its worn texture.
summary: A distressed single-weight serif based on a historic Dutch body-text sample, originally released in 1999 and since reissued.
description: Augustinian keeps the worn, printed texture of its Dutch source material rather than cleaning it up into a crisp revival, giving roman and italic a lived-in editorial character.
foundry_blurb: Famira Fonts describes Augustinian as based on a historic Dutch body text sample, originally released in 1999 and recently reissued through Type Network.

name: Interpol Correspondence
classification_notes: A faux typewriter face with ink-trap-driven closed apertures and non-standard proportions, classified as slab for its typewriter-slab structure despite not being truly fixed-width.
summary: A faux typewriter face built to pair with Interpol Sans, with wide spacing, ink traps and non-standard proportions rather than true fixed-width.
description: Interpol Correspondence takes on a typewriter's closed apertures and wide spacing through expansion contrast and ink traps, with a wide lowercase i and l bearing serifs against a narrow M and W. It supports Greek and Cyrillic alongside Latin.
foundry_blurb: Famira Fonts describes Interpol Correspondence as a faux typewriter style to pair with Interpol Sans, not fixed-width, with all Interpol styles carrying Greek and Cyrillic support.

name: Interpol Sans
classification_notes: A robust, low-contrast humanist sans engineered for legibility at low resolution, on screens, in projection and on lightboxes.
summary: A robust, low-contrast humanist sans designed by Hannes Famira in 1992 for legibility on screens, lightboxes and projections.
description: Interpol Sans consumes noticeably less space than classic proportions would suggest, a thrifty quality that lets it fit more words per line than a typical sans without feeling cramped. Type Network cites an exceptionally high reading rate for the design.
foundry_blurb: Famira Fonts describes Interpol Sans as a stylistically strong but modest humanistic sans serif with an exceptionally high reading rate, designed for confidence wherever legibility is essential.

name: Basilea
classification_notes: A distressed blackletter whose letterforms were traced directly from a shipping box, part of the Jetsam Collection anthology of grunge typefaces built from found objects rather than historical blackletter sources.
summary: A distressed blackletter traced from the lettering on a shipping box that once held Egyptian t-shirts.
description: Basilea pairs a solid, bold uppercase with a skinny lowercase that fizzles out toward the baseline, effectively two fonts in one. It includes superior figures and abbreviation symbols for street, place and avenue, and belongs to Famira's Jetsam Collection anthology of grunge typefaces.
foundry_blurb: Famira Fonts describes Basilea as a distressed blackletter font whose letter shapes were taken from a shipping box that contained t-shirts from Egypt, part of the Jetsam Collection anthology of grunge typefaces.

name: Jupette
classification_notes: A cheeky, slightly soft sans-serif channelling the French Riviera around 1956, sitting between geometric and humanist construction.
summary: A cheeky, slightly soft sans breathing the spirit of the French Riviera around 1956, in five weights with italics.
description: Jupette covers book covers, editorial design, packaging and branding with equal ease, its ten styles running Light to Ultra with matching italics. A streamlined Jupette Grotesk sibling simplifies the shapes for a more neutral finish.
foundry_blurb: Famira Fonts describes Jupette as breathing the spirit of the French Riviera round about 1956.

name: Jupette Grotesk
classification_notes: A streamlined, more neutral companion to Jupette, with simplified shapes, unified proportions and squared-off terminals in place of Jupette's soft curves.
summary: A streamlined, more neutral companion to Jupette, with simplified shapes and squared-off terminals.
description: Jupette Grotesk keeps its parent's Riviera-era spirit but flattens the counters, straightens the terminals and squares off the corners for a plainer, more general-purpose grotesque across five styles.
foundry_blurb: Famira Fonts describes Jupette Grotesk as a streamlined version of Jupette, with simplified shapes, more unified proportions, terminals that cut off horizontally and corners that are not rounded.

name: Keiko Titling
classification_notes: A heavyweight titling face rebuilt from Famira's 1990s FontShop release ffBlocker, meant for headlines rather than text.
summary: A clean-outline titling face rebuilt from Famira's 1990s FontShop release ffBlocker, with an expanded weight range.
description: Keiko Titling updates ffBlocker's bold, impactful letterforms with wider language coverage and a fuller weight range, aiming, in the designer's words, at the sweet spot between quiet legibility and a recognisable style.
foundry_blurb: Famira Fonts describes Keiko Titling as featuring clean outlines with 'fatter is better' as the guiding idea, updated from the 1990s FontShop release ffBlocker with expanded weights and language coverage.

name: Mutilated
classification_notes: A capitals-only display face digitised from little rubber stamps printed in Chinese ink on rough paper, Famira's first released typeface.
summary: A capitals-only grunge display face digitised from rubber stamps printed in Chinese ink, Hannes Famira's first released typeface.
description: Mutilated started life as a set of little rubber stamps found in a supermarket toy department, printed by hand and digitised into a range of five weights, of which two, Plain Caps and Fat, were released by FontFont in 1994.
foundry_blurb: Famira Fonts describes ffMutilated as released in 1994 as a FontFont, Hannes Famira's first typeface, its shapes taken from rubber stamps printed with Chinese ink on rough paper.

name: Sonar Sans
classification_notes: A geometric sans that deliberately avoids strict symmetry, marrying geometric construction with the forgiving character of early gothic typefaces.
summary: A geometric sans that marries strict geometric form with the forgiving, human expression of early gothic typefaces.
description: Sonar Sans uses geometry as a starting point rather than a rule, so nothing about the design is truly symmetrical, giving it a low-contrast, approachable presence suited to branding and corporate identity work.
foundry_blurb: Famira Fonts describes Sonar Sans as marrying geometric, historical form with the forgiving, human expression of early gothic typefaces, noting that nothing about the design is truly symmetrical.
